name: aladdin.colors
description: Canonical Aladdin color tokens for 'The Aperture'. Primitives are fixed hex; semantic tokens are theme-aware and reference primitives via {primitives.<name>}. This file is the source of truth; DESIGN.md frontmatter, frontend/src/styles/tokens.css, and the Tailwind theme mirror it.
maintenance: Manually maintained. On any color change, edit this file first, then propagate to DESIGN.md frontmatter and frontend/src/styles/tokens.css (see tokens/README.md).

basalt.description: Dark canvas / Admin default; warm-neutral graphite-black stone.

basalt-3.description: Highest dark surface step; secondary fills on dark.

limestone.description: BRAND stone. The Aperture mark, the auth Brand Panel, and the primary button label. No longer the light canvas.

plaster.description: BRAND stone. No longer the raised surface on light.

sand.description: BRAND stone. No longer the secondary fill on light.

quartz.description: Light canvas; the brand stone with the chroma removed (channel spread 4, vs 10 for Limestone). Warm, never cream.

quartz-sunk.description: Secondary fills, tags, chips on light.

quartz-hover.description: Pointer-over ground on light; one step short of quartz-sunk so a hovered row reads as armed and the current row still reads stronger.

quartz-line.description: Hairline border on Quartz. Luminance-matched to line-light within 0.0003, so it keeps that border weight while dropping two-thirds of the chroma.

quartz-line-strong.description: Strong border on Quartz. Luminance-matched to line-light-strong.

ink.description: Primary action fill on light; near-black.

lumen.description: Brand / AI point-of-light; glows and large fills.

lumen-deep.description: Supporting Lumen shade for larger marks on light.

lumen-ink.description: AA-safe Lumen tone for normal-size text/strokes/focus on light.

lumen-soft.description: Light Lumen tint for gradients and soft glow stops.

bronze.description: Trust/verification metal; seals and premium detailing.

bronze-deep.description: Bronze for larger marks on light surfaces.

bronze-ink.description: AA-safe Bronze tone for normal-size trust text and small seals.

lapis-bright.description: Lapis on the Basalt dark theme.

verdigris-deep.description: AA-safe success tone for normal-size text on light.

verdigris-bright.description: Success on the Basalt dark theme.

ochre-deep.description: AA-safe warning tone for normal-size text on light.

ochre-bright.description: Warning on the Basalt dark theme.

oxide.description: Danger (oxide red); AA on light and larger marks.

oxide-bright.description: Danger on the Basalt dark theme.

stone-muted.description: Quietest light text that still clears AA on the canvas/surface (not on the secondary fill).

line-light.description: BRAND hairline, retained as a primitive. Superseded as the light semantic border by quartz-line.

line-light-strong.description: BRAND strong hairline, retained as a primitive. Superseded by quartz-line-strong.

on-dark.description: Primary text on dark; also dark-theme primary action fill.

shell.description: THE WORKSPACE SHELL — the sidebar's own material. An architectural blue, deliberately NOT the enterprise navy #001537 it replaced (hue 217 at 100% saturation, sampled off a rendered concept, derived from nothing in this palette). Chrome only: never a content surface, never a card, never a page ground.

shell-lit.description: Head of the shell ramp. The active navigation row is a wash of THIS (white 14%), not of the page's ground — a near-white pill on a saturated rail reads as pasted on rather than carved out.

shell-pool.description: The tonal pools painted inside the shell.

shell-dark.description: The shell in dark theme. Only MODERATELY darker than the dark workspace — light theme keeps a large gap between the two materials, dark theme deliberately does not, or the page becomes one undifferentiated near-black stack.

shell-dark-lit.description: Head of the dark shell ramp.

shell-dark-deep.description: Foot of the dark shell ramp.

shell-dark-pool.description: Tonal pools inside the dark shell.

shell-text.description: Primary text ON the shell. Tinted from the shell's hue rather than grey — a neutral grey on a saturated ground reads as dirty.

shell-text-muted.description: Group headings and quietest chrome on the shell.

mineral.description: THE WORKSPACE ATMOSPHERE base (light) — the cool-mineral field the whole B2B page is composed on. Light on purpose: the SIDEBAR carries the ink, and a large expanse of low-luminance colour was twice rejected as a workspace ground for reading as heavy.

mineral-lit.description: The tone the atmosphere's pools are mixed TOWARD. Never mix toward white — that produces a spotlight, and a room is not a spotlight.

mineral-dark.description: Atmosphere base in dark theme. A soft charcoal-ink, deliberately neither pure black nor the app's own near-black carbon.

mineral-dark-lit.description: Pool mix target in dark theme.

navy-air.description: A TINT SOURCE, never a surface. Tinting a light ground toward a near-black blue yields grey, not blue: navy (0,21,55) mixed into a light ground at 15% gains barely 9 points of blue-minus-red. This is the same hue carried up to PAGE lightness, and it is what the atmosphere's seam pool — the sidebar's own hue diluted by the room — is actually mixed from.

navy-edge.description: The second, quieter atmosphere pool's hue. Tint source only.

fg-muted.note: AA only on canvas/surface; NOT on the secondary fill quartz-sunk (4.47:1). See the Muted-On-Sunk Rule.

primary-foreground.note: Brand stone on ink. Unchanged by the Quartz move: neither token in this pair is the canvas.

accent-solid.note: Glows/fills/large marks only; not normal-size text on light.

shell.note: Chrome family. Separate from surface/canvas ON PURPOSE: these are the only tokens allowed on chrome, and surface/canvas the only ones allowed on content, so the two can never be confused at a call site.

shell-fg-muted.note: Group HEADINGS only — uppercase 11px, which is not body text. Never use for a readable label.

shell-active.note: The carved active row. A wash of the shell's OWN lit tone, never the page ground, and it carries no cast shadow — a dark shadow under a light-on-dark wash is a smudge, not a depth cue.

shell-active-fg.note: The rail's full-strength foreground, NOT an inverted ink: an ink tuned for a near-white pill is close to invisible on a translucent wash of the shell.

workspace-pool-cool.note: The SEAM pool — the sidebar's own hue. This one token is the mechanism behind the sidebar reading as integrated with the environment rather than pasted beside it.

workspace-pool-warm.note: The one warm note in a cool field. Restrained — the brand's accent, not a second temperature competing with it.

workspace.note: The operational ground the cards are drawn on. Panels stay `surface`.

shell-fg.note: The dark theme's own primary text. Literal rather than a {primitives.*} reference because the Carbon ramp it belongs to is not in this file yet — see knownDrift.

shell-active.note: SAME percentage as light, and that is correct rather than lazy: the token it mixes FROM already carries the theme, so re-deriving the percentage on top double-counts it. Measured at 9% and the active row visibly flattened against the rail.

workspace-pool-cool.note: Hues are theme-independent; only the mesh they mix INTO changes, so the same percentages land as a tint rather than a glow.

workspace.note: The Carbon ground. Literal for the same reason — see knownDrift.

knownDrift.note: PRE-EXISTING, NOT INTRODUCED BY THE SHELL PASS. This file still names Basalt as the dark canvas/surface ramp; the implementation (frontend/src/styles/tokens.css) moved the dark GROUND to a neutral Carbon ramp some passes ago — Basalt was retained as a brand colour only. The Carbon primitives, the dark elevation shadows and the scrollbar tokens are therefore absent here. The shell/workspace family added on 2026-08-26 IS current. Reconciling the dark ramp is its own task; do not treat the Basalt entries above as authoritative for the dark workspace.
knownDrift.authority: frontend/src/styles/tokens.css is currently ahead of this file for the dark theme.
